Tasks.Prompt: For a given line l with C on it, construct a perpendicular through C. For a separate marked angle CBA, first estimate a midpoint D by eye, then construct ray BX that bisects angle CBA with compass/straightedge; compare to D and ask a partner to critique the tool sequence. Submit both drawings and written equal-radius reasons.

Criteria.Criterion: Perpendicular correctly through C, with symmetric A,B on l and valid arc openings
Estimates D before constructing valid internal angle-bisector ray BX
Justifies perpendicular/right angle and bisected angle with radii/equal sides, not appearance
Uses precise verbal tools, completes partner critique and compares estimated vs constructed

Tasks.Accept: Any nondegenerate angle below 180 degrees, either equivalent arc intersection/orientation; correct labels and proof
Tasks.Reject: Digital screenshot claimed from unimplemented tool, typed number-only, skipped estimated D or one unsupported visual angle split

Tasks.Prompt: With an unmarked straightedge and compass construct a line perpendicular to l at C and an angle bisector for an independently given angle AOB. Explain why both are correct and distinguish the 180-degree straight-angle case.

Criteria.Criterion: Valid two-intersection auxiliary circle/arc construction for perpendicular through C
Line passes through C with marked right angle
Angle bisector from vertex O using equal marks and equal arcs
Written geometric justification for both equal angles and 180-degree relation

Tasks.Accept: Actual labelled paper construction with explanation and right-angle mark
Tasks.Reject: Numerical angle answer or guessed ray without tool-defined equalities

SourcePracticeAnalogues.Mode: Four current and four spiralling first-party questions, all human-reviewable with exact source-skill roles (not original source images)

Items.Prompt: Line l contains A,C,D in that order with AC=CD. Why is a perpendicular bisector of AD guaranteed to pass through C?
Items.Expected: C is the midpoint AD by AC=CD; its perpendicular bisector passes through midpoint C.

Items.Prompt: For angle PQR, let S,T be points on QP and QR with QS=QT and U be an interior point satisfying SU=TU. What conclusion follows about QU and angle PQR?
Items.Expected: Triangles QSU and QTU are congruent by SSS (QS=QT, SU=TU, QU common); QU bisects angle PQR.

Items.Prompt: Two equal circles centred A and B pass through each other's centres and intersect C,D. Why is A-C-B-D a rhombus?
Items.Expected: AC=CB=BD=DA=AB from the two radius-AB circles, so four equal sides.

Items.Prompt: In a regular hexagon centred O radius r, do six central triangles OAB,OBC,... have all equal sides? Explain.
Items.Expected: Each chord of adjacent vertices equals radius r, so each central triangle has three sides r.

Items.Prompt: Two circles centred A and B both radius r. E lies on circle A, C lies on circle B. Which lengths equal each other?
Items.Expected: AE=BC=r because each is a radius of a congruent circle.

Items.Prompt: If CD is a perpendicular bisector of AB crossing at M, compare MA and MB, and justify.
Items.Expected: MA=MB because M is midpoint; all points on perpendicular bisector are equidistant from A and B.

Items.Prompt: A paper sheet is folded so distinct A,B overlap exactly. Explain why every point on the fold is equidistant from A and B.
Items.Expected: A fold acts as reflection exchanging A and B; crease fixed points have equal distances and form perpendicular bisector.

Items.Prompt: Circle centred C passes through B and D; must CB=CD? Explain.
Items.Expected: Yes, CB and CD are radii of the same circle.

AuthoringStageC.PaperHandoff: Student draws perpendicular through given C and angle bisector through vertex B, labels estimated D and exact ray BX; gives diagram and partner critique to authorized school teacher. Teacher marks each 0/1/2 criterion, totals 0–8, acknowledges with date/signature on paper; no online grade asserted.

Cases.correct: symmetric points and perpendicular through C plus valid radius-arc bisector with reason
Cases.equivalent: alternative legal compass openings or rotated/reflected correctly labelled angles
Cases.wrong: eye-only ray D accepted as exact or incorrect perpendicular through point
Cases.insufficient: number or unlabeled figure without written reasoning and paper construction
Cases.malformed: 0/180 angle treated as a non-degenerate interior bisector or undefined vertex
